statement: SK Hynix is in preliminary talks with Intel to make HBM and advanced DRAM at Intel's Ohio fab, which would be SK Hynix's first US memory manufacturing; no investment size or timeline was disclosed.
why: HBM is the tightest input in the accelerator bill of materials; any credible addition of HBM/DRAM wafer capacity, and a US location that trims tariff and logistics friction, points to more memory supply behind future GPU builds.

impact.mechanism: Using Intel Ohio capacity would add HBM/advanced DRAM output outside Korea, easing the memory constraint on merchant-GPU assembly and validating Intel Foundry as an external-customer supplier.

evidence.excerpt: SK Hynix is in talks with Intel about manufacturing memory chips at Intel's Ohio fabrication facility.

confidence.basis: Secondary restatement of a Reuters report resting on unnamed sources; talks are explicitly preliminary with no finalized agreement and no figures.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend unknown -> unknown); sources: HotHardware
